clinician.trajectory_summary: A 41-year-old asymptomatic female underwent screening mammography and was found to have incidental calcifications in the periareolar region of the right breast. Magnification views demonstrated numerous round and punctate calcifications in a regional distribution in the right subareolar breast, predominantly in the skin with extension into the nipple. Physical examination revealed no visible or palpable abnormality overlying the radiographic findings. A breast radiologist used the mammograms to localize the skin microcalcifications, and the patient underwent incisional biopsy of the marked site. Histopathological evaluation of the biopsy specimen revealed multiple small but variably-sized fragments of foreign material with angulated and refractile appearance consistent with glass shards on a background of scar tissue. Follow-up clinical discussion with the patient confirmed a history of motor vehicle accident with chest trauma several years earlier, providing the clinical context for the pathological findings of embedded glass from the shattered windshield.
